transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-21
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 43 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Reyes (Redwood SE), Eve Cho (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (Aurelia), Dana Ortiz (Aurelia NetOps), Priya Menon (Aurelia Security), Leo Grant (Aurelia SRE)

Auto-generated summary (short):
Redwood and Aurelia reviewed week-2 bakeout results for the Redwood Private on-prem pilot. Main topics: p95 latency regressions during concurrency spikes, KV cache hit rates, quantization kernel mismatch on older GPUs, and a proposed fallback playbook that routes to a lighter model variant when KV misses exceed threshold. Security asked for audit log retention and KMS rotation details. Action items and next steps agreed to run a 24hr traffic replay and schedule a dry run.

Topics covered:
- Bakeout test results and anomalies
- KV cache and prefix caching behavior
- Quantization/kernel compatibility on customer GPUs
- Fallback routing playbook and circuit breaker thresholds
- Security/compliance questions (SOC2, KMS, SAML)
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, um quick roll call then we'll jump into the numbers.
[00:07] Samir Patel: hi, Samir here, good to be back.
[00:10] Dana Ortiz: Dana from NetOps.
[00:11] Priya Menon: Priya, security.
[00:13] Leo Grant: Leo, SRE.
[00:15] Marcus Reyes: Marcus from Redwood engineering.
[00:18] Lena Park: cool. we left off last week with the bakeout run — Marcus, you wanna open with the headline results?
[00:26] Marcus Reyes: yeah, quick summary. 24 hour run across three racks, roughly 2.1M tokens ingested, average throughput held steady but we saw p95 spikes coincident with concurrency bursts from replay. p95 moved from ~120 ms to ~260 ms in those windows. p99 similarly spiked. the KV cache hit rate was about 78% overall but dropped to 42% during the bursts, which lines up with the latency increase.
[00:48] Samir Patel: just to clarify, those bursts are from the traffic replay script we ran that simulates your peak hour, correct?
[00:53] Marcus Reyes: correct. also important: when KV hit rate fell, the runtime fell back to the larger model variant in a couple of cases because of our policy match — so that path increased token cost and added compute scheduling delays.
[01:09] Dana Ortiz: are you saying Redwood automatically flipped models? i thought that was manual.
[01:13] Marcus Reyes: no it's policy — there's a routing rule that says if latency or queue depth crosses threshold, route to a cheaper-latency optimized variant; in our config we had a variant with fewer layers and higher quant which trades quality for latency. seems like the routing thresholds need tuning.
[01:30] Lena Park: ok, so two levers: improve KV caching and tweak fallback thresholds. Marcus, any quick fixes?
[01:36] Marcus Reyes: short term: bump max-prefix cache size and reduce eviction timer, which should raise hit rate maybe 6–10%. long term: pre-warm KV caches for known prefixes during peak windows. also noticed quan‑tization kernel mismatch on your older Ampere cards — the runtime fell back to a slower generic kernel which added ~40ms per token in some paths.
[01:58] Priya Menon: can you say quan‑tization mismatch again? our security person wants exact wording for the ticket.
[02:02] Marcus Reyes: sorry, quan‑ti— quan‑ti za tion kernel: in a nutshell, our optimized INT8 kernel requires driver level support present in more recent CUDA builds; if driver doesn't report AVX/patch or if the GPU reports slightly different architecture string we default to a safe slower path. we'll capture the exact driver strings in the artifact.
[02:26] Leo Grant: just to add, some of our older nodes still run the vendor's older firmware, we had planned a firmware refresh this quarter but it's been delayed. could that be the main cause?
[02:34] Marcus Reyes: yes likely. firmware/driver mismatch is primary cause for the slow kernel fallback.
[02:37] Samir Patel: what's the impact if we don't update firmware before cutover?
[02:41] Marcus Reyes: expect a consistent 10–25% latency overhead and higher token cost because of slower execution — but not correctness issues.
[02:49] Dana Ortiz: ok, so we should plan firmware in our dry run.
[02:52] Lena Park: noted. switching gears — telemetry and observability: did the instrumented traces capture queue depth correlation?
[03:00] Marcus Reyes: yes, the trace correlates request queue depth at the load‑balancer with KV misses. i pushed a perf sheet link into the chat — see the 'burst-heatmap' tab.
[03:10] Lena Park: great. Priya — security questions?
[03:13] Priya Menon: quick list: audit log retention (we need 3 years), KMS key rotation policy (90 days), and SAML assertion expiration defaults. also whether Redwood stores plaintext request payloads in any logs.
[03:24] Lena Park: good questions. short answers: logs are encrypted at rest, we can support export to your KMS; default SAML assertion TTL is 1 hour but can be tuned; we don't persist plaintext request bodies in long‑term logs unless you opt in for debugging; i'll send the full security pack and SOC2 attestation after this call.
[03:43] Priya Menon: please include whether audit logs can be forwarded to our SIEM and format (json/cef).
[03:49] Eve Cho: we do forward in JSON and can set up a direct collector if needed.
[03:53] Leo Grant: on the fallback playbook — can you outline thresholds and how automatic reroute works? we need a circuit breaker we can inspect and roll back quickly.
[04:02] Marcus Reyes: current logic: breaker trips on sustained p95 > 200ms for 2 consecutive minutes OR queue depth > 80% for > 30s. on trip, routing policy prefers a latency-optimized variant in same pool or in a dedicated pool if available. the rollforward is immediate; we also emit a continuous event so you can auto-trigger scaling or alerts.
[04:23] Dana Ortiz: 2 minutes seems long to us, our ops prefer shorter to avoid user impact.
[04:27] Lena Park: we can parameterize that — propose we try 45s for the test replay and see behaviour.
[04:33] Samir Patel: agreed to 45s for next run.
[04:36] Marcus Reyes: noted — change will be in the routing policy in the perf spreadsheet, i'll also add a repeatable terraform snippet so you can spin the same policy locally.
[04:45] [05:00] Speaker 1: (unintelligible)
[05:03] Leo Grant: small nit — if you route to a different model variant does the client see a different model_id? we need to ensure telemetry label consistency.
[05:12] Marcus Reyes: yes model_id changes but we emit a canonical 'service_model' tag in traces so downstream aggregations remain coherent. we'll make sure the tag is present in all paths.
[05:25] Priya Menon: can you commit to not changing that tag without notice?
[05:28] Lena Park: yes, we have back-compat guarantees for telemetry tags during pilot windows.
[05:33] Samir Patel: quick question on data residency — if we fall back to Redwood hosted variant in a different region during surge, does any payload leave our VPC?
[05:42] Marcus Reyes: by default, the fallback variant would run in your Private cluster; only if capacity is exhausted would policy escalate to a Redwood-hosted fallback, and that requires explicit customer opt-in in the pilot. we had opted 'no-hosted-fallback' in your config.
[06:00] Dana Ortiz: good, keep it explicit.
[06:03] Lena Park: jumping to action items recap later. Marcus, anything else on perf anomalies?
[06:08] Marcus Reyes: one more: we observed ~0.6% request failures during the spikes — primarily TCP retransmits and a handful of 5xxs from the model runtime when queue depth exceeded process limits. recommended mitigation: small autoscale buffer + circuit breaker tuning.
[06:25] Leo Grant: what's the suggested autoscale buffer?
[06:28] Marcus Reyes: ~12% headroom for steady state, with 30% burst capacity that can be spun within 90s.
[06:34] Samir Patel: spin within 90s is... depends on your scheduler. are we booting GPUs or reuse warm instances?
[06:41] Marcus Reyes: we prefer warm spare capacity for sub-2min spin up; for this pilot we can reserve a small dedicated pool of warm nodes.
[06:49] Dana Ortiz: that costs more, will need finance sign off.
[06:52] Lena Park: understood — we'll add cost delta in the follow-up sheet.
[06:56] [06:59] Speaker 2: (overlap)
[07:02] Priya Menon: security follow up: about KMS, are you OK with BYOK?
[07:07] Marcus Reyes: yes, we support BYOK and HSM integrations; we will provide steps and the entropy requirements.
[07:12] Priya Menon: and the rotation timeline again?
[07:14] Lena Park: default rotation 90 days but we can align to your 60/90 policies.
[07:18] Priya Menon: perfect.
[07:20] Marcus Reyes: also, i'll attach the driver/firmware strings to the perf artifact so you can map which nodes will see the slow kernel path.
[07:27] Dana Ortiz: can you also include the minimal CUDA/driver versions?
[07:30] Marcus Reyes: yes, minimal supported CUDA 11.8 with the hotfix we mention; full compatibility matrix in the sheet.
[07:37] Lena Park: ok, timeline — we want to run a 24 hour traffic replay with changed parameters: prefix cache bump, breaker 45s, warm pool 12% headroom. Samir, Dana — can you run that and share traces?
[07:48] Samir Patel: yes, we'll schedule starting 2026-09-25 02:00 UTC and run 24 hours.
[07:54] Dana Ortiz: noted.
[07:56] Lena Park: great. two other items: run the on‑prem cutover dry run and firmware plan. propose dry run 2026-10-02, firmware refresh schedule TBD but earlier the better.
[08:08] Leo Grant: 10/02 works for dry run, firmware might slip, we'll keep you posted.
[08:13] Marcus Reyes: meanwhile, for immediate gains we can ship the routing tweak and cache config as a patch; i'll push a PR to your staging config repo if you give me access.
[08:24] Samir Patel: give access to samir@aurelia.health, i'll approve.
[08:28] Lena Park: noted.
[08:30] [08:31] Speaker 3: (laughs)
[08:33] Priya Menon: one compliance nuance — audit trail needs to show model variant change events, is that doable?
[08:40] Marcus Reyes: yes, we already emit model-change events with timestamps and reason codes, we'll surface them in the forwarded logs.
[08:46] Priya Menon: add retention policy to the pack please.
[08:48] Lena Park: will do.
[08:50] Marcus Reyes: quick note on cost math — when we routed to the smaller layer model during the bursts we actually saw higher cost because the scheduling delay increased tokenization window, we will add a line item in the cost sheet showing per‑token delta for fallback events.
[09:06] Samir Patel: helpful.
[09:08] Lena Park: ok let's go to final recap and owners.
[09:12] Marcus Reyes: recap: 1) Marcus to bump cache defaults and add kernel strings to artifact, 2) Marcus to change breaker to 45s and add terraform snippet, 3) Marcus to add cost delta lines, 4) Lena to send security pack and SOC2, 5) Aurelia to run 24h replay and share traces, 6) schedule dry run 2026-10-02.
[09:34] Dana Ortiz: confirmed.
[09:36] Priya Menon: confirmed on security items.
[09:38] Lena Park: perfect. i'll follow up with a calendar invite for the dry run and share the updated perf sheet and security pack within 48 hours.
[09:45] Samir Patel: thanks folks, this was productive.
[09:47] Marcus Reyes: thanks, we'll get those artifacts out today.
[09:50] Lena Park: meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
